AI-powered business automation

How AI agents took over routine customer requests and repetitive internal workflows, giving teams back the time they had been spending on manual, low-value work.

Let's Talk All case studies
Sector
Operations
Focus areas
  • AI agents
  • Workflow automation
Related
AI & automation · Business automation
Client
Confidential
Overview

Many organisations reach a point where their people spend more time moving information around than using it. That was the situation here: customer support and internal operations relied on the same repetitive steps being performed by hand, day after day. We introduced AI agents to handle the routine work automatically, so the team could focus on the questions and decisions that genuinely need a person.

The challenge

What needed to change

Customer support and internal workflows depended on repetitive manual work.

None of the individual tasks was difficult. The problem was volume and repetition: the same requests, the same look-ups and the same hand-offs, handled one at a time by people whose skills were being used for routine work.

What was getting in the way

  • Routine requests filling the queue

    Straightforward, repeated customer questions took up the same attention as the complex ones.

  • Manual hand-offs between steps

    Internal processes relied on people passing work along by hand, which created waiting time and room for things to be missed.

  • Skilled people on repetitive tasks

    Team members spent a large share of their day on work that followed the same pattern every time.

  • Hard to scale

    Handling more requests meant adding more manual effort, because the work itself was not automated.

The solution

What we delivered

We built AI agents that handle routine customer requests and automate internal workflows.

The agents take on the predictable, repeatable part of the work: recognising common requests, responding to them, and moving internal tasks through their steps without someone having to push them along. People stay in charge of the work that needs judgement.

Key capabilities

  1. 01

    Automated handling of routine requests

    AI agents recognise and respond to common customer requests without manual effort.

  2. 02

    Workflow automation

    Repetitive internal steps run automatically, so work moves forward without manual hand-offs.

  3. 03

    People where they add value

    Complex, sensitive or unusual cases remain with the team, who now have more time to give them.

  4. 04

    Consistent responses

    Routine requests receive the same accurate handling every time, whoever would otherwise have picked them up.

  5. 05

    Room to absorb growth

    Higher volumes of routine work can be handled without the same increase in manual effort.

Our approach

What shaped the solution

The priorities that guided the design and delivery.

  • Automate the routine, not the judgement

    We focused the agents on the predictable, repeatable work and kept people responsible for anything that needs context or care.

  • Fit the existing operation

    Automation was designed around the way the team already worked, so it removed steps rather than adding new ones to learn.

  • Start where the repetition is highest

    Effort went first to the requests and workflows that consumed the most manual time.

The impact

What changed for the business

  • Routine work handles itself

    Common requests and repetitive internal steps no longer depend on someone being available to process them.

  • Teams focus on higher-value work

    Time that went into repetitive tasks is now available for customers and problems that need human attention.

  • A more scalable operation

    The organisation can take on more routine volume without the same growth in manual workload.
